clinician.trajectory_summary: A 53-year-old male presented with acute abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, and focal peritonitis, along with highly elevated WBC (38.4 x 10^9/L) and platelet counts (691 x 10^9/L). Initial workup included an abdominal CT scan which found no source of infection or contrast leak. A peripheral blood smear showed severe leukocytosis and thrombocytosis without circulating blasts. Subsequent bone marrow biopsy revealed slightly hypercellular marrow (70%) with evidence of trilineage hematopoiesis, mild myeloid and megakaryocytic hyperplasia, and molecular evidence of BCR/ABL + fusion, confirming the diagnosis of CML, chronic phase.
